Strategies by Timeframe: Scalping, Intraday, Delivery

On this page

  2. 1. Scalping (seconds to ~5 minutes)
  3. 2. Intraday (minutes to hours, squared off by the close)
  4. 3. Delivery: swing and positional (days to months)

Which strategies fit scalping, intraday and delivery (swing/positional) trading on NSE, the equations behind each, and what the evidence and my own backtests say. Related: strategies_from_equations.md (full rules for the 5 core strategies), using_equations_to_trade.md (pass/fail tests and sizing), trading_equations.md (formulas). Education, not investment advice.

The deciding factor: costs vs. the size of the move

Round-trip costs from my Fyers cost model (projects/trading experiments/supertrend_di_backtest.py, 2026 charges), before slippage:

Trade valueIntraday round tripDelivery round trip
₹50,000₹53 (0.11%)₹173 (0.35%)
₹1,00,000₹83 (0.08%)₹284 (0.28%)
₹5,00,000₹225 (0.05%)₹1,174 (0.23%)

Add slippage of roughly 0.02–0.03% per side for liquid large caps.

Break-even win rate once costs are included:

$$p^{*} = \frac{L + c}{W + L}$$

W = average win, L = average loss, c = round-trip cost + slippage, all in % of the trade.

StyleTarget WStop LCost cBreak-even win rate (no costs → with costs)
Scalp0.20%0.10%0.13%33% → 77%
Intraday1.0%0.5%0.13%33% → 42%
Swing (delivery)6%3%0.34%33% → 37%

Costs barely matter on a 6% swing move but are most of a 0.2% scalp. This is the main reason SEBI found 70%+ of intraday cash traders lost money in FY23, and 80% of those making 500+ trades a year lost (projects/trading experiments/indian_market_strategies_research.md).

1. Scalping (seconds to ~5 minutes)

Verdict: not recommended for a retail trader in Indian cash equities.

  • Needs a ~75%+ win rate just to break even at 2:1 reward-to-risk (table above).
  • Professional scalping is really market making (Avellaneda–Stoikov, eq 19) and order-flow trading, with exchange co-location, fee rebates and millisecond execution. Retail can't compete there.
  • My own tests: MACD+RSI+Stoch lost on 5m with every exit; SuperTrend+DI "best" cells didn't survive 0.02–0.03% slippage.

If scalping anyway (index options/futures), the equations that matter:

  • Break-even win rate (above) — compute it before every strategy.
  • Order-book imbalance: $\text{OBI} = \dfrac{Q_{\text{bid}} - Q_{\text{ask}}}{Q_{\text{bid}} + Q_{\text{ask}}}$ (top-of-book quantities; > 0 means buying pressure).
  • Hard daily loss limit (e.g. stop for the day at −1% of capital).

2. Intraday (minutes to hours, squared off by the close)

Verdict: possible, but only with few trades a day, liquid stocks, and strict loss limits. Test every idea with costs + slippage first. Evidence for these is mostly gross of costs.

a) Opening range breakout (ORB) on "stocks in play"

  • Equations: relative volume $\text{RVOL} = \dfrac{\text{volume in first 15 min today}}{\text{avg volume in first 15 min, last 20 days}}$; ATR (eq 10) for stops; fixed-fractional size (eq 8).
  • Rules: opening range = high/low of 09:15–09:30. Trade only stocks with RVOL > 2 (news, results). Buy a break above the range high (short below the low), stop at the other side of the range or 0.1 × daily ATR, exit at the close or a 2R target. Max one trade per stock per day.
  • Evidence: Zarattini & Aziz reported +0.13R per trade on QQQ, but gross of spread/slippage; an independent replication on five indices found the edge reproduced gross but net ≈ zero. Restricting to stocks in play is what the stronger results rely on.
  • Book: Grimes Art and Science of Trading (course workbook) ch.15 "The Opening Range Phenomenon" (books/trading/, pdf p533).
  • Mine: NY ORB gold strategy (ny_orb_v1_backup.pine) exists but has no written report yet.

b) Intraday momentum (first half-hour → last half-hour)

  • Equation: $r_{\text{first}} = \dfrac{P_{09:45}}{P_{\text{prev close}}} - 1$ predicts $r_{\text{last}}$ (15:00 → 15:30).
  • Rules: at 15:00, go long Nifty futures if $r_{\text{first}} > 0$, short if < 0; exit at 15:25. Optionally only on high-volatility or high-volume days, where the effect was stronger.
  • Evidence: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (Journal of Financial Economics 2018) on the S&P 500 ETF, 1993–2013; international results are mixed and I found no Nifty-specific study → must be backtested here.
  • Why it's attractive: one trade a day, so costs stay small.

c) VWAP mean reversion (range days only)

  • Equations: $\text{VWAP} = \dfrac{\sum P_i V_i}{\sum V_i}$; stretch $z = \dfrac{P - \text{VWAP}}{\sigma_{\text{intraday}}}$.
  • Rules: on days without a strong trend (e.g. first-hour range below average), fade moves with |z| > 2 back toward VWAP; stop at |z| > 3; no new trades after 14:30.
  • Evidence: I found no rigorous after-cost study — only indicator scripts. Treat as untested.

d) Intraday pairs

Cash-market shorting is allowed intraday, so pairs (eq 15–16) can run without futures. But Indian research found pairs profitable in stock futures, not in the cash market, because of costs. Only worth testing with a slow-moving, wide spread.

Intraday risk rules (all strategies)

  • Risk 0.25–0.5% of capital per trade; stop for the day at −1% to −2%.
  • At most 2–3 trades a day; only liquid large caps or index futures.
  • Check the break-even win rate for each strategy's actual W, L and costs.

3. Delivery: swing and positional (days to months)

Verdict: the best fit for a retail trader. Moves are big relative to costs, trades are few, and the strongest evidence in Indian equities is here. My own backtests also did best on daily charts.

StrategyHolding periodMain equationsNotes
Momentum portfolio + vol targeting~1–3 months per stock, monthly rebalancerisk-adjusted momentum score, 1/σ weights (eq 9, 11)Strongest evidence (IIM-A: ~21–22%/yr, 1994–2014). Full rules in strategies_from_equations.md #1
Quality / low-volatility factorsmonthsfactor scores, σ (eq 11), beta (eq 5)Strong evidence; smoother than momentum; blend with it
Volatility-managed NiftyongoingMerton fraction + GARCH (eq 7, 12)A better buy-and-hold. Rules in #2
Swing trend breakout (daily)days–weeksATR stop (eq 10), position size (eq 8), expectancy (eq 1)e.g. my Tori daily Break: 51.5% win, 2R, profitable on 13/13 symbols, but rarely beat buy-and-hold → check alpha (eq 5)
Daily MACD with "MACD crosses down" exitdays–weeksexpectancy, Sharpe, drawdownMy Reliance test: PF ~1.5–1.7 after delivery costs on daily — needs out-of-sample and multi-stock test
Pairs trading via stock futuresdays–weeksz-score, OU half-life (eq 15–16)Indian study: profitable in futures 2011–2017 after costs, not in cash

Delivery rules of thumb: risk 0.5–1% per position with an ATR-based stop; hold 10–20 positions; size by volatility; rebalance on a schedule, not on feelings; always compare with a Nifty index fund.

Summary

StyleUse it?Best strategiesWhy
ScalpingNo (for retail cash)— (market making needs infrastructure)Costs require ~75%+ win rate; my 5m tests lost
IntradayMaybe, few trades a dayORB on stocks in play, intraday momentum on Nifty futuresEdges are thin and mostly gross of costs; must backtest net
Delivery / swingYesMomentum + vol targeting, quality/low-vol, vol-managed Nifty, daily trend breakoutsBig moves vs costs; strongest evidence; my best results

Tax note (check current rules before relying on it): intraday equity profits are taxed as speculative business income at slab rates; delivery gains are capital gains (short-term under 1 year, long-term above, at lower rates). This also favours longer holding.
